name: Dow Inc.
moat_justification: Real scale and integration advantages that lower Dow's position on the cost curve — vertically integrated megasites (Freeport, Terneuzen) that cannot be replicated quickly, and a U.S. Gulf Coast ethane/propane feedstock advantage over naphtha-based peers — but the core products are undifferentiated commodities sold on price, returns are set by the global capacity cycle and Chinese additions, sustaining capex runs at roughly D&A, and the feedstock edge is a spread that can narrow. No durable pricing power through the cycle: FY2025 prices fell faster than feedstock costs and normalized owner's earnings went negative.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
one_liner: Integrated commodity-chemical giant, moat 4/10, but normalized conservative owner's earnings are negative (−$0.26/share median base; FY2025 OE −$1,601M as OCF no longer covers capex through the downcycle) — Tier F on this screen; no hurdle-clearing price is computable on a negative OE base.
moat_for: Vertically integrated megasites (Freeport TX, Terneuzen) — internal conversion avoids intermediary margins and freight; permitting alone blocks quick replication
U.S. Gulf Coast ethane/propane feedstock advantage vs naphtha-based international peers — higher ethylene yields, costs less tied to crude
Top-tier global scale and supply reliability for large customers (alongside LyondellBasell, ExxonMobil Chemical)
Specialty pockets with more customer stickiness — silicones, polyolefin elastomers, coatings in Performance Materials & Coatings
moat_against: Core products are undifferentiated commodities bought on price; low switching costs outside specialty grades
No pricing power through the cycle — FY2025 polyethylene prices fell faster than feedstock costs, margins compressed to trough
Global overcapacity, especially Chinese capacity additions, sets the marginal price
Ethane advantage is a commodity spread that narrows when oil/gas ratios move
Heavy sustaining capex (capex ≈ D&A) plus recurring restructuring/impairment charges are structural, not one-offs
Legacy liabilities keep surfacing — Sadara guarantee, DuPont/Corteva indemnifications, litigation
